metadata.title: Bidirectional Recurrent Neural Networks as Generative Models

extraction_notes.note: The experimental evidence is in tables (NLL per data set) and figures; the tables and figure captions are not nodes, and the claims read off them carry rigor numerical.

Data-set descriptions and hyperparameter choices in Sections 5.1-5.2 (one-hot d=96 encoding, sequence lengths, hidden sizes, learning-rate grid, music data details) and future-work sentences without mathematical content were left as text.
Baselines and evaluation protocols described in prose were typed as algorithms; AP4 (one-way inference) is a single operation and gets zero steps.

The Bayesian MCMC description spans the Bayes'-theorem derivation; the derivation sentence with Eq. (8) is a nested claim and the algorithm steps are the Gibbs-sampling and proposal-enumeration sentences around it.

nodes.statement: Let us denote the input to a recurrent neural network by X = leftlbrace x_t rightrbrace where x_t in R^N is an input vector for each time step t.

Let us denote the input to a recurrent neural network by $\mathbf{X} = 
\left\lbrace \mathbf{x}_t \right\rbrace$ where $\mathbf{x}_t \in \mathbb{R}^N$ 
is an input vector for each time step $t$.

nodes.statement: Our first probabilistic interpretation is thus that the joint distribution defined by a BRNN is the asymptotic distribution of a process that replaces one observation vector x_t at a time in X by sampling it from P_BRNN(x_t mid \x_d\_dneq t).
nodes.raw_latex:
Our first probabilistic interpretation is thus that the joint distribution 
defined by a BRNN is the asymptotic distribution of a process that 
replaces one observation vector $\mathbf{x}_{t}$ at a time in $\mathbf{X}$ by 
sampling it from $P_{\mathrm{BRNN}}(\mathbf{x}_{t} \mid \{\mathbf{x}_d\}_{d\neq t})$.
nodes.clean_text: Our first probabilistic interpretation is thus that the joint distribution defined by a BRNN is the asymptotic distribution of a process that replaces one observation vector x_t at a time in X by sampling it from P_BRNN(x_t mid \x_d\_dneq t).

nodes.statement: The joint distribution of the time series is defined by first drawing a random permutation o_d of time indices 1dots T and then setting data points observed one by one in that order, starting from a fully missing sequence: P_NADE(Xmid o_d) = prod_d=1^T P(x_o_d mid \x_o_e\_e=1^d-1).
nodes.raw_latex:
The joint 
distribution of the time series is defined by first drawing a random permutation 
$o_d$ of time indices $1\dots T$ and then setting data points observed one 
by one in that order, starting from a fully missing sequence: 
\begin{align}
P_{\mathrm{NADE}}(\mathbf{X}\mid o_d) = \prod_{d=1}^T P(\mathbf{x}_{o_d} \mid \{\mathbf{x}_{o_{e}}\}_{e=1}^{d-1}).
\end{align}
nodes.clean_text: The joint distribution of the time series is defined by first drawing a random permutation o_d of time indices 1dots T and then setting data points observed one by one in that order, starting from a fully missing sequence: P_NADE(Xmid o_d) = prod_d=1^T P(x_o_d mid \x_o_e\_e=1^d-1).

nodes.name: Negative Log Likelihood (NLL) over the test data for the trained models. As a comparison, similar numbers are presented for the unidirectional RNNs trained by citetboulanger2012modeling
nodes.statement: caption Negative Log Likelihood (NLL) over the test data for the trained models. As a comparison, similar numbers are presented for the unidirectional RNNs trained by citetboulanger2012modeling and by citetNIPS2013_5166. The results serve as a sanity check that the trained models have been trained successfully. Note that the BRNN has more context than the unidirectional RNNs, and is hence expected to perform better measured by NLL. Also note that the training of the model for NADE without masking is very similar to the training of the BRNN. textwidth@extracolsepfill l c c c c c hlinenoalign Inference strategy & Wikipedia & Nottingham & Piano & Muse & JSB \\ noalign hline noalign NLL of BRNN & 0.37 & 3.23 & 6.82 & 5.68 & 7.80 \\ NLL of NADE masked & 0.55 & 3.32 & 7.42 & 6.48 & 8.51 \\ NLL of NADE & 0.41 & 2.89 & 7.05 & 5.54 & 7.59 \\ NLL of unidirectional RNN & 1.21 & 3.87 & 7.88 & 7.43 & 8.76 \\ citetboulanger2012modeling & & 4.46 & 8.37 & 8.13 & 8.71 \\ citetNIPS2013_5166 & 1.12 &&&& \\ hline
